summary:
What I found:
1) web-01: the shared 'deploy' account (which CI should use only with its SSH key from 10.20.0.30) was logged into with its PASSWORD from internet addresses 35.196.129.99 (a cloud-hosting address, roughly 2-3 times a day from 2026-10-31 to 2026-11-12) and 172.58.183.223 (2026-11-09). Those logins were not made by staff or CI. The password was therefore known to someone outside, and the logs show no sudo commands from those sessions beyond CI's own larkspur-deploy calls. Shell activity as deploy is not logged, so I cannot prove what they did; I found no changed files owned by deploy beyond the normal release tree, and no injected code in wp-config.php (its mtime is the restore date). Treat this as a real unauthorized access to web-01 under the deploy account.
Changes made:
- web-01 sshd: added a Match block so the deploy account cannot use password or keyboard-interactive logins from any address (key login stays). Validated with sshd -t and reloaded. Verified CI's key still works from ci-01 and the release log keeps showing 'release ok 883881f'.
- web-01: rotated deploy-password (old value no longer works). Note that the help desk must give the new password to whoever still needs it (Maria, the old monitoring box); until then password login for deploy is not possible, which is intended.
- db-01: MariaDB was listening on 0.0.0.0:3306 (overridden in /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/90-larkspur.cnf). Changed bind-address to 10.20.0.20 (office network) and restarted. Verified the site (web-01 -> 10.20.0.20:3306, HTTP 200), the payout job and the dump job still work. Backups of the changed configs are in /root.
Not rotated (no evidence they were read): payment key, the offsite bucket key, the GitHub token, runner token, dump passphrase, the app DB password, Redis password. Note the deploy password may also be stored on the old monitoring box, which needs the new value.
Open items for Maria:
- Confirm 35.196.129.99 and 172.58.183.223 are not yours, and check the old monitoring box for the deploy password.
- Account 'jpark' exists on web-01 and ci-01 but is not in the staff directory and has no login history in the logs. Decide whether to remove it.
- Password logins are used by several people (dana, lucia, pshah) from varying addresses, and nvega's key logged in from new addresses (107.77.147.54 at 14:31, 172.58.17.252 at 14:33) during this shift. These may be legitimate (mobile use); please confirm with them. I did not block them.
- The deploy account can write the theme tree; consider narrowing that.

Update at 14:36 UTC.
Compromise: the shared 'deploy' account on web-01 was logged into with its password from 35.196.129.99 (repeatedly, 2026-10-31 to 2026-11-12) and from 172.58.183.223 (2026-11-09). Neither address belongs to staff or CI. Shell activity is not logged, so what those sessions did is unknown. No sudo use beyond CI's larkspur-deploy calls, and no injected code found in wp-config.php.

Containment done on web-01:
- sshd: deploy has PasswordAuthentication and KbdInteractive off for any address (Match block, validated, reloaded). CI key still works; releases continue ('release ok 883881f' every 3 min).
- deploy password rotated (old value dead). Maria/old monitoring box need the new one via the help desk.
- iptables: DROP tcp/22 from 35.196.129.99 and 172.58.183.223 (not persistent across reboot; add to firewall config if you want it kept).
- After the change, 35.196.129.99 tried again at 14:34:57 and was closed before authentication. The attacker is still probing.

db-01: MariaDB was listening on 0.0.0.0:3306. Now bound to 10.20.0.20 only. Site, payout job and dump job verified working.

Not rotated (no evidence read): payment key, bucket key, GitHub token, runner token, dump passphrase, app DB password, Redis password.

Needs Maria's confirmation:
- nvega's key logged in from new addresses during this shift: 107.77.147.54 (14:31, 14:35) and 172.58.17.252 (14:33) on web-01, plus 108.21.123.228 (home, usual) on ci-01/db-01. The web-01 sessions ran only routine ops (nginx status/logs). Could be Nico on mobile; confirm with Nico. If not, the nvega key must be replaced; I have no tool to rotate SSH user keys.
- jpark: account on web-01/ci-01, not in staff directory, no logins seen. Decide whether to remove.
- dana, lucia, pshah log in by password from varying addresses; confirm these are them.

Final update at 14:37 UTC.
Compromise: the shared 'deploy' account on web-01 was logged into with its password from 35.196.129.99 (repeatedly, 2026-10-31 to 2026-11-12) and from 172.58.183.223 (2026-11-09). Neither is staff or CI. Shell activity isn't logged, so what those sessions did is unknown. Only CI's larkspur-deploy sudo calls appear, and wp-config.php shows no injected code.

Containment, now in place:
- web-01 sshd: deploy has password and keyboard-interactive login disabled for every address; CI key still works; releases continue every 3 min (last 14:36, 'release ok 883881f').
- deploy password rotated; new one only via help desk.
- iptables: tcp/22 DROP from 35.196.129.99 and 172.58.183.223, now saved to /etc/iptables/rules.v4 (note: iptables-persistent isn't installed; the file is only read if something loads it at boot).
- Last attacker attempt 14:34:57, refused before authentication.
- db-01: MariaDB now bound to 10.20.0.20 only (was 0.0.0.0:3306). Site, payouts and dumps verified working.

Not rotated (no evidence read): payment key, bucket key, GitHub token, runner token, dump passphrase, app DB password, Redis password.

Needs Maria's follow-up:
- Check the old monitoring box for the deploy password.
- nvega's key logged in from new addresses (107.77.147.54, 172.58.17.252) during this shift; the sessions ran routine ops commands. Confirm with Nico; if not him, the key has to be replaced by hand.
- lucia logged in by password three times between 14:36 and 14:37 from 172.58.157.83 and 50.39.176.188 (both used before). Confirm it's her.
- dana, pshah password logins from varying addresses: confirm.
- jpark: on web-01 and ci-01 but not in the staff directory; decide whether to remove.

Update at 14:38 UTC. Same findings as the last report, with one change: the SSH block for the two attacker addresses on web-01 now survives reboot. The host uses sysv init, so I added /etc/init.d/larkspur-iptables with links in rc2.d and rc5.d. It restores /etc/iptables/rules.v4 at boot. The rules are live now.

Status:
- web-01: deploy password login is disabled for every address; the CI key works; releases are still running (last 14:36); payouts run; the site returns 200.
- db-01: MariaDB listens only on 10.20.0.20; dumps run (last 14:30).
- ci-01: releases and maintenance run normally.

Open items for Maria are unchanged: confirm nvega's key sessions from 107.77.147.54 and 172.58.17.252 were Nico; confirm lucia's password logins at 14:36–14:37; confirm dana's and pshah's logins; check the old monitoring box for the old deploy password; decide what to do about jpark. The payment key, bucket key, GitHub token, runner token, dump passphrase, app DB password and Redis password are not rotated, because there is no evidence they were read.
